It can show as study you complete, an important thing finally put into clear words, or a sibling matter brought to an honest end. With neighbours it might be the long-running issue over the fence finally sorted. Pick one piece of learning or one conversation and take it all the way to done.
3.reversed:
In the third house, The World reversed tends to leave a thought circling that won't close. There's a conversation you keep rehearsing and never have, a course left half done, a mental loop that won't come to a point. Without Saturn's structure, the quick Gemini side of this house runs on without landing, and Mercury, its ruler, will happily keep talking forever.

You'll see it in courses started and dropped, messages drafted and never sent, and a sibling or neighbour issue talked around for years. Short trips carry it too, the errand you've meant to run for months. An open loop drains you quietly, so you can end up scattered and tired without knowing why. Close one. Send the message, finish the module, or say the thing to your brother or sister.

4.upright:
The fourth house is home. The actual house or flat, the family you came from, and the private ground you go back to when everything else is done. It's angular, one of the chart's corners, so what happens here shapes everything built on top of it. The World in this house is a home or a family chapter coming to a real close. There's friction to name, though. The house's natural sign is Cancer, ruled by the Moon, and Saturn is in detriment in Cancer, working against the grain of everything soft and familial this house stands for.

So the completion on offer is the harder kind. A family pattern seen through to its end, a home put together with patience when warmth wanted to skip the practical parts. Capricorn sits opposite Cancer, just as the fourth house sits opposite the tenth, and you may feel that tug between home and career quite sharply. Finishing something tender can feel cold, as if you've stopped caring. You haven't.

It can show as the house finally made solid, the renovation done, the mortgage paid down. With parents it can be making peace with where you came from, or finishing a role you've played in the family since you were small. It can also be a move. Choose the one family conversation you've avoided and have it.
4.reversed:
Roots that won't settle are the usual story of the fourth house with The World reversed. A domestic chapter that's neither closed nor properly begun, a family matter left dangling, a home that never quite feels like solid ground. Saturn already strains in this Cancer house, and reversed it shows as a family cycle you can't bring yourself to end, or a house built on foundations that were never finished.

It shows as the move that never feels like arriving, boxes still unpacked a year later, a parent issue reopened at every holiday, and the past quietly unsettling the present. Something at the base is unfinished. Go back and deal with it before you build any higher, including the difficult last part.

5.upright:
The fifth house is where you play. Creativity, romance, children, hobbies, anything done for the pleasure of it. It's succedent, a house that builds up and holds, it belongs naturally to Leo and the Sun, and Venus has her joy here, so it's meant to be warm and spontaneous. The World brings a planet that would honestly sooner work than play. Saturn's detriment is in Leo, and it's uncomfortable in all this fire and fun, so the completion this card offers comes with some friction.

That friction can be the making of something, though. A creative gift only turns into a body of work when patience finishes what the spark started, and a romance only grows into something lasting when someone commits to the dull parts too. You might find you're more serious about your hobbies than usual, or that a relationship that started as fun is asking to be taken seriously. The worry is that finishing drains the fun. Usually it doesn't.

With a creative project this can be the painting, the album, the novel actually done and shown. With romance it's a love that grows up. With children it can be a stage of their lives finishing, and you getting to see who they've become. Finish one creative thing you love and put it in front of someone.
5.reversed:
A creative or romantic circle that won't close is what The World reversed usually means in the fifth house. A project stalled at ninety percent, a romance held back from where it wants to go, a pleasure you keep putting off because finishing it feels like pressure. Saturn's discomfort in this Leo house shows as either a critic in your head freezing the fun, or a perfectionism that won't let something playful just be done.

It shows in half-finished art you won't show anyone, a love you won't fully commit to, a hobby that's turned into homework. With children it can mean pushing them to finish things you never finished yourself. Finish the thing badly if you have to, and go back to doing it for fun afterwards.

6.upright:
The sixth house is the daily round. The work you actually do each day, the routines that keep you going, the body's upkeep, the dishes and the dog walk. It's cadent, a house of adjustment and service, and Virgo is the sign that goes with it, ruled by Mercury. The World fits here well. Capricorn, Saturn's home, is earth like Virgo and trines it, and Saturn likes exactly what this house is made of, repetition, structure, the long dull upkeep that holds a life together.

The theme is a routine seen all the way through. The habit that finally sticks after years of false starts, a working day that's settled into something you can sustain, a body looked after by consistency and not by crisis. Mars has its joy in the sixth, which adds some appetite for effort, and with The World here that tends to mean steady physical work, the gym habit that holds, the garden dug over properly. The small risk is turning upkeep into a list of boxes to tick.

At work it can be a system you built that now runs itself. With your health it's the result of years of dull good choices. With pets or anyone you care for daily, it's care that's become second nature. Finish setting up one daily routine properly, and then stop tinkering with it.
6.reversed:
The routine gets left unfinished when The World sits reversed in the sixth house. A health plan dropped just before it became a habit, a way of working that never quite settles, the body's upkeep left at ninety percent so the gains keep slipping. Saturn wants the boring maintenance carried all the way through, and reversed that discipline breaks down into good intentions that don't survive a busy stretch.

It shows as the fitness plan restarted again and again, admin piling up, and small daily jobs skipped until they turn into bigger ones. At work it can look like a desk nobody else could find anything on. Make the habit small enough to keep, five minutes, one glass of water, one walk round the block, and don't add anything until it's automatic.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite you. A partner, a business partner, anyone you've made a serious one-to-one agreement with. It's angular, one of the chart's corners, so things here tend to move. And this is about the best house The World could land in. The seventh's natural sign is Libra, ruled by Venus, and Saturn is exalted in Libra, welcomed and working at its most ideal. In relationships Saturn is commitment, the vow, the contract, the person who's still there in year fifteen.

Maturity is the thing here, in how you join up with someone. The card describes a bond that has lasted through a full cycle and proved it can carry weight, love or work built slowly and honestly. Even here there can be a threshold to cross, a commitment actually made, or an ending finished cleanly. Exalted Saturn gives you the backbone for either one, and Venus, ruling the house, keeps it kind.

With a partner this could be moving in, marrying, or renewing something that's been taken for granted. In business it's the contract signed with clear eyes, or a partnership formalised after years of handshakes. With a long relationship it might simply be noticing that it's become whole. Tell your partner, plainly, what you think the two of you have built.
7.reversed:
The World reversed in the seventh house usually means a bond sitting just short of whole. A commitment put off, a partnership neither deepened nor ended, something important held at a threshold nobody will cross. Saturn is strong in this Libra house even reversed, so the backbone is there. It's going unused, and you circle the decision without making it. Venus rules Libra and wants to keep the peace, so the limbo can feel pleasant enough to go on for years.

It shows as the partner you won't fully commit to and won't leave, the contract left unsigned, and the ending both of you avoid because closing it feels like failure. In business it can be a partnership that's run its course and still has both your names on it. Make the real choice this relationship is asking for, and tell the other person what you've decided.

8.upright:
The eighth house is what you share with other people at the deepest level. Joint money, debts, inheritances, the mortgage in two names, and intimacy, including sex. It's also where the big endings live. It's succedent, a house that builds and holds, and its natural sign is Scorpio, ruled by Mars in the old system. The World brings its clean, structural sort of ending into a house that already knows a lot about endings, and it's a good pairing. Saturn's home sign, Capricorn, is sextile to Scorpio, a cooperative angle, and Saturn knows how to close a cycle properly.

The completions here happen where it matters a great deal. A shared financial tangle finally settled, closeness that's matured into real trust, an ending faced squarely. Aquarius squares Scorpio, and that's where the friction comes in, a pull to keep things cool and at a distance when the house is asking for depth. There's often a control question in it too, the urge to manage a change that really needs to be allowed to happen.

With joint money it can be sorting accounts so they're fair and clear. In intimacy it's closeness that's grown unhurried and whole. With loss, it's grief you finally let run its course. Get the shared paperwork into one place, both names, all the figures, and go through it together.
8.reversed:
Deep cycles resist closing with The World reversed in the eighth house. A transformation with loose ends trailing, a shared-money matter that's festering, an intimacy or an ending you grip instead of finishing. Saturn wants the boundary drawn so the deep work can end, and reversed it turns into a refusal to let go that you might call strength.

It shows in an inheritance or joint account left in an ugly limbo, closeness stalled by fear of being fully known, and grief you won't allow to run its course. Mars rules this house traditionally, and when it's frustrated it comes out as arguments about money that are really about trust. Pick the one shared matter that's been left longest, and put a date on finishing it.

9.upright:
The ninth house is the long view. Belief, study, far travel, the search for what your life means, anything that takes you past your usual streets. It's cadent, a house of learning, Sagittarius sits here in the natural chart, ruled by Jupiter, and the Sun has its joy in the ninth. It's naturally about expansion. The World brings the discipline that turns all that seeking into something finished. Saturn gives Jupiter's big questions some structure, so a belief gets tested into real conviction and a course actually reaches its end.

What's live is a philosophy or a faith that's grown into something you can stand on, and the reward of having followed the long questions all the way. Capricorn sits next to Sagittarius, neighbours with little in common, and that's the tension, a house that loves the open horizon being asked to arrive somewhere. Aquarius is sextile to Sagittarius, and it helps through other people, a teacher, a study group, a friend overseas.

It can show as a degree or a training finished, a belief you've lived in long enough to trust, a trip that changes you because you let it finish its work. With publishing or teaching, it's the book done or the course written. Choose one search you care about and bring it to a real conclusion, even a provisional one.
9.reversed:
The ninth house under a reversed World tends to circle a conclusion it won't quite reach. A course left incomplete, a belief taken up loudly and never tested, a search for meaning that keeps moving so it never has to land. Saturn wants the long inquiry carried to its end, and reversed it can look like restlessness passing itself off as an open mind. Jupiter rules this house and always has a bigger idea waiting.

It shows as a degree dropped near the end, seeking that avoids committing to any real answer, and travel that collects experiences and makes sense of none of them. It can show with in-laws or a faith community, too. Finish the inquiry you actually care about, and write down what you've concluded so far.

10.upright:
The tenth house is the top of the chart. Your career, your public role, your reputation, what people know you for. It's angular, the most visible of the four corners, and its natural sign is Capricorn, with Saturn as natural ruler. So The World is on home ground here, the card of completion drawn at the top of the mountain with its own planet ruling the house. It points to a career or a public achievement actually reaching the place it was always headed.

Arrival in the outer world is the theme. Years of unglamorous effort becoming visible, a reputation that rests on real, finished work. The tension, and it's a real one up here, is the pull to start climbing the next thing straight away before this one has been properly taken in. Saturn rewards the long build, and it also asks that the finish be marked, the chapter closed properly, the handover done well.

In your job it can mean a promotion, a qualification recognised, a project with your name on it completed and seen. It can mean stepping out of a role at the right time, having done it fully. With your public standing it's being trusted because you've earned it. Mark the finish somehow, a dinner, a proper handover, a line on your CV, before you look for the next thing.
10.reversed:
In the tenth house, The World reversed often means a career sitting at ninety percent of the summit. Recognition delayed, a goal hovering just short, or a role you've outgrown and keep clinging to. Saturn is powerful in the house it rules, so reversed the block is usually self-made, a finish you keep deferring or a title you won't hand back.

It shows in the promotion that never quite lands, credit that lags behind the real work, and a position you've mastered and should be leaving cleanly. It can follow you home, too, the job coming through the door with you every evening. People around you may see the end of this role before you do. Decide which it is, and take one step toward claiming what you've done or stepping down from it.

11.upright:
The eleventh house is your wider circle. Friends, groups, networks, the club, the online community, and the hopes you're working toward. It's succedent, a house that builds and holds, and its natural sign is Aquarius. People often forget that the eleventh's traditional ruler is Saturn, so The World is on home ground again. Jupiter rejoices in this house as well, which adds some luck and generosity to the mix.

Belonging that has matured is the heart of it, the difference between a crowd of contacts and a handful of people who'll turn up when it counts. The card points to a community or a shared hope brought to a real finish, friendships that have proved themselves over years, a network that holds because it was built patiently. The tension is that this house looks to the future, and it's being asked to honour something that's already whole.

With friends it can be a group that's quietly become chosen family. With a cause or a club it's a long-term goal reached with other people, the fundraiser hit, the building opened. With your hopes it's recognising that one of them has actually come true. Tell the friends who've been there longest what they mean to you, in person if you can.
11.reversed:
The World reversed in the eleventh house tends to mean a circle that won't close. A shared hope stalled short of whole, a friendship chapter left unfinished, a network you keep widening because you can't face going deeper. Saturn rules this house traditionally, even with the card upside down, so what's usually missing is follow-through, the difference between knowing people and building something lasting with them.

It shows in causes you join and drift from, friendships kept shallow across a wide field, and a shared plan everyone talks about and nobody finishes. Being busy with lots of people can leave you oddly alone. Pick one friendship or one group and give it what it actually needs, or let a long-held group hope be honestly retired.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the hidden room. Sleep, dreams, retreat, the unconscious, the things you do in private and the things you don't quite admit to yourself. It's cadent, a house of letting go, and Pisces is its natural sign, ruled by Jupiter, Neptune in the modern system. Saturn has its joy in the twelfth, which surprises people. The planet of limits does its best work in the house of solitude, and that makes this one of The World's strongest placements, in a quiet way.

What's live is a completion happening below the surface. A long inner chapter coming full circle where nobody can see it, sometimes including you. An old pattern that finally stops, a grief worked through in private, some peace after a hard stretch alone. The tension is trusting a finish you can't point to or prove. Saturn's discipline helps here in plain ways, a regular bedtime, a daily quiet hour, a retreat that's been booked and paid for.

In sleep it can show as nights that finally feel restful. With private grief it's letting the ending happen without explaining it to anyone. In caring roles, a hospital, a hospice, a relative's bedside, it can be quiet work that means more than it looks. Protect one regular block of time alone and don't fill it.
12.reversed:
An inner chapter stays open under a reversed World in the twelfth house. A private matter left unfinished, something buried you won't look at directly, a vague feeling of not quite belonging that follows you around without a name. Saturn does its best work in this house, so the loss is real, a completion that's available in private and keeps getting avoided by staying busy.

It shows in grief you never let yourself feel fully, an old hurt steering things from underneath, and the retreat you keep needing and keep putting off. Dreams can keep going back to the same house or the same person. People around you may only see the busy version. Give the hidden work some real solitude, a day with nothing in it, and let it finish.
